population.note: FICTIONAL. Totals: ~270M adults. On drug: 21.4% ≈ 57.8M. Ever used: 31.0% ≈ 83.7M. Used and now off: 31.0 − 21.4 = 9.6% ≈ 25.9M. Never used: 69% ≈ 186M. Flow arithmetic, using the parent world's rates (≈50% two-year persistence, 55% two-year restart): of the 18.8 pts on in 2030, 9.4 stayed on and 9.4 stopped. The off pool became 7.7 + 9.4 = 17.1, and 55% of it restarted (9.4). Earlier ever-users on now: 9.4 + 9.4 = 18.8. New ever-users: 31.0 − 26.5 = 4.5, of whom 2.6 are on and 1.9 already off. On: 18.8 + 2.6 = 21.4. Off: (17.1 − 9.4) + 1.9 = 9.6. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030, plus ~4.0 pts of first-time restarts, gives 12.9 of 31.0 = 42%. Generic entry in 2032 did not raise persistence within the window, because the bone warning and the 'grey' complaint pushed planned stops and drug holidays up about as much as the lower price reduced cost-driven stops. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 2.4 + 7.92 + 8.28 + 2.76 = 21.4. 65+ is flat at 12% (~7.45M) because new generic starters offset stops after the 2031 fracture communication. Income thirds: (26 + 21.5 + 16.7)/3 = 21.4. Bottom-third growth (13 → 16.7) comes mostly from $45–69 generic semaglutide paid in cash. The remaining non-users in that third are mainly uninsured adults for whom $588/yr is still real money, plus people who opted out. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, of whom ≈150k are aged 6–11 (liraglutide on-label; generic semaglutide off-label under pediatric endocrinology). Children in a typical classroom now include several on a drug and many with parents on one.

access.public_coverage: The structure is unchanged. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge ran through 2031 and was carried through 2032 in a routine December 2031 health-extenders package, with the same $275/month per-user payment, $50 copay and criteria, plus the 65+ DEXA/strength counselling visit. About 2.2M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 2.2M × $275 × 12 ≈ $7.3B/yr. Because the payment is a fixed per-user rate, plans earn a margin on Bridge users switched to generic semaglutide. Overall, Medicare pays ≈13.5% of incretin fills ≈ 7.8M users (7.45M aged 65+ plus ~0.4M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈10.5% ≈ 6.07M users. About 3.0M were moved to generic semaglutide at ~$60 net through ordinary generic substitution, and 3.07M remain on branded agents at ~$275: (3.0M × $60 + 3.07M × $275) × 12 ≈ $12.3B/yr combined, down from $18.2B. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program continues under flat full-year continuing resolutions at $4.5B. Its 2.0M liraglutide users × $85 × 12 = $2.04B, plus 1.18M cessation/AUD semaglutide users × $58 (after the contract price-reset clause triggered on generic entry) × 12 = $0.82B, total ≈ $2.86B, leaving ~$1.6B unobligated.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month and has approved generic tirzepatide. China sells generic semaglutide and branded mazdutide domestically. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in ~180 countries. In the US, generic semaglutide injection is available from Jan 2032 (patent expiry plus settlement terms). There is no US generic tirzepatide or oral semaglutide.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~57.8M users: commercial 34% (19.7M), Medicare 13.5% (7.8M), Medicaid 10.5% (6.07M), HRSA free provision 5.5% (3.18M), cash/direct 20% (11.56M), gray 16.5% (9.54M); total 100%, 57.8M. The cash share rose because generic semaglutide at $45–69 now undercuts many plans' $50+ specialty copays and gets around weight-loss exclusions. People with insurance are buying the drug outside it, so who pays changed in volume but not in structure. Prices: generic semaglutide injection runs $45–69 cash across eight ANDA holders plus Novo's authorised generic. TrumpRx cut tirzepatide to $349 in Mar 2032. Orforglipron (Foundayo) is $149. Retatrutide came off allocation in Nov 2031 and is $649 on LillyDirect; its list price is $1,499. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, kept for rebate contracts. Gray composition has shifted toward next-gen molecules, because generic semaglutide wiped out the price case for compounded semaglutide: compounded 'personalised' tirzepatide ~4.0M ($99–149), research-use retatrutide including 16 mg-equivalent vials ~2.5M ($90–180), Chinese-made mazdutide and other 'research' triples ~1.0M ($60–120), and residual compounded or imported semaglutide ~2.0M. Generics are exempt from the Section 232 tariff, so Indian-made generic semaglutide reaches US pharmacies legally.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; US generics from Jan 2032)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 16 mg maintenance dose from Apr 2031)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, Oct 2031)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
alcohol use disorder (semaglutide FDA-approved Jun 2030; tirzepatide guideline-endorsed Oct 2031, sNDA under review)
gambling disorder (semaglutide, ASAM/APA guideline-endorsed Oct 2031; sNDA accepted, PDUFA date Q2 2033)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic semaglutide for gambling disorder and compulsive buying, prescribed by addiction clinics ahead of the label and mostly paid in cash
low-dose 'focus/quiet' subscriptions, now repackaged generic semaglutide; shrinking under complaint and FTC pressure
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
'metabolic health' and longevity regimens with DEXA and strength coaching
research-peptide retatrutide and mazdutide for 'recomposition' in gyms
compulsive screen use and pornography reduction, sold by telehealth 'digital sobriety' brands, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The ~30% triple-agonist driver is realised as an existing product in a new form, as the approval rules require. In Apr 2031 the FDA approved a retatrutide 16 mg maintenance dose on the TRIUMPH extension data: 30.4% mean loss at 96 weeks, with a stronger body-composition and bone monitoring section. Lilly's new Concord and Lebanon lines lifted allocation in Nov 2031. MariTide (BLA filed Jul 2030) was approved in Oct 2031 for monthly dosing at ~17–20% loss, with ~0.6M users by late 2032. Survodutide's resubmission went to a split advisory committee in Jun 2032 on the hepatic signal, and no decision has been made. Amycretin was resubmitted in Feb 2031 but is held behind reinspection of Novo's North Carolina site, with a decision expected Q1 2033. Lilly filed its bimagrumab + tirzepatide muscle-preservation combination in Sep 2032, now marketed to investors as the answer to the bone and muscle warning, with a decision no earlier than late 2033. The compulsion indication exists as a guideline endorsement plus a filed sNDA, not an FDA label. The US incretin market shrank in price and grew in volume: global incretin revenue ≈ $128B in 2032, the first annual decline. Novo's US semaglutide revenue is down roughly 45%, and Lilly holds the next-gen tier.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Higher rates with retatrutide 16 mg and with gray-market tirzepatide and retatrutide escalated without titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; generic labels carry identical text.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Persistence after discontinuation remains disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~58,000 claims. After a split second and third bellwether in 2031, Novo began global settlement talks. Generic-maker liability is limited by federal preemption doctrine for generics.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label; Novo settlement framework under negotiation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute terms with 30% loss on retatrutide 16 mg and with research-peptide use.
No causal confirmation in long-term data; low absolute risk. About 8,000 claims sit in the MDL.

Now treated as a population problem. In Medicare data, sarcopenia criteria are met ~1.6× more often after more than 2 years of use, and the fall-related ED visit excess is measurable in 65+. Worst among unmonitored generic and liraglutide users with low protein intake. Retatrutide 16 mg trials show lean-mass loss of ~38% of total loss without training.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Sep 2031 class Drug Safety Communication: body composition moved into Warnings and Precautions. Resistance training and protein counselling are recommended for all long-term users ≥50. The HRSA programme still has no body-composition requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A 2031 Medicare claims analysis of ~6.1M beneficiaries found hip fracture HR 1.42 after 2+ years and among cyclers, concentrated in women. Applied to ~4.5M long-term 65+ users at ~0.5%/yr baseline incidence, that is ≈9–10k excess hip fractures and ≈35–40k excess fragility fractures a year. The authors give ~2,000 excess deaths a year as an upper bound at conventional post-hip-fracture mortality.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Sep 2031 Drug Safety Communication recommends baseline and biennial DEXA for long-term users ≥50 and all postmenopausal women. DEXA waitlists of 3–5 months in many metros. No dose or duration limits imposed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; unchanged, including in AUD and gambling trial populations.

In Mar 2031 the retatrutide postmarketing study reported dose-dependent anhedonia-scale (SHAPS) shifts, clinically meaningful in ~7% at the top dose versus ~2% on placebo. Surveys still put reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users across agents. 'Drug holidays' are common: an estimated 30% of long-term users skip at least one dose a quarter on purpose.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to the retatrutide Adverse Reactions section in 2031. No class warning. The FTC consent order with two 'focus' brands (2031) bars 'side-effect-free calm' claims. The guideline endorsements for AUD and gambling cite the same mechanism as therapeutic.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now also driven by planned stops after the fracture communication and by drug holidays that turn into lapses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation ongoing; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, vitamin D and B12 insufficiency signals strengthen, linked in the bone literature to fracture risk in older low-income users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; folded into the 2031 DSC counselling language.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of adult and ~nine years of adolescent follow-up; ~150k children aged 6–11 on a drug.
An interim registry readout (Jun 2032) shows smaller-than-expected gains in BMD Z-score among adolescents on drug for 3+ years, in a non-randomised comparison confounded by weight loss itself.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA calls the data 'not interpretable for labelling'; final bone-accrual study due 2034.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Calls shifted from semaglutide to tirzepatide and triple agonists. Poison-centre incretin calls are up a further ~40% since 2030. CBP seizures of Chinese 'research' triples tripled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts on Chinese peptide exporters; ~60 warning letters; first federal indictment of a peptide distributor (Jun 2032); still no prosecution of individual users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Higher at the 16 mg dose (~6%) and in research-peptide users.

food_and_beverage.state: With more than one adult in five on the drug and cheap generics reaching bottom-third households, volume losses in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks continue at about the 2030 rate. Discount-channel losses are now steeper than premium ones. Majors finish selling indulgent brands to private equity. Protein, fibre, calcium and vitamin-D-fortified formats grow faster after the bone warning.

alcohol.state: The tirzepatide AUD endorsement and $45–69 generic semaglutide reach heavy drinkers who never had parity coverage. Spirits volume is down again and beer contracts. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' formats grow. State excise forecasts for alcohol, tobacco and gaming are revised down together.

restaurants.state: The sector has settled into smaller plates, protein-forward menus and fewer drinks. Value-volume chains have finished their unit closures. Las Vegas resorts report lower beverage and gaming spend per room night, and higher spend on spa and shows.

apparel.state: Size runs stabilise. 'Athletic cut' is still growing. A new market in hip protectors and 'balance' footwear for older users emerges after the fracture communication.

fitness.state: The DSC made resistance training medical advice. Strength studios run Medicare Advantage 'bone programmes' and DEXA vans tour retirement communities. The gym-floor gray market in retatrutide and mazdutide continues.

insurance.state: The structure is unchanged. Pharmacy trend falls from ~+14% to ~+6% as plans add generic-semaglutide step therapy. Employer weight-management coverage drifts to 58%, mostly by putting generic semaglutide in the 'covered' tier. More members bypass coverage altogether by paying cash, which leaves PBMs less adherence data than before.

pharma.state: Novo loses roughly half its US semaglutide revenue to generics and its own authorised generic, and is in MDL settlement talks. Lilly owns the next-gen tier (retatrutide 16 mg, tirzepatide, Foundayo) and has filed bimagrumab. Indian generic makers that are exempt from the tariff win US share. Global incretin revenue falls for the first time while volume rises.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug carries no signal any more. Being off it does. A heavy body at 40 invites the question 'did you stop?', and the polite answers are 'bone scan', 'pregnancy' or 'drug holiday'. The finish is still read as a class marker. A 30%-loss retatrutide body with muscle reads as a coach and a DEXA subscription. A thin, soft body reads as a $49 generic pen and no time for the gym.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The price gap has mostly closed and the monitoring gap has not. In Sun City, Arizona, the retirees who can pay for DEXA and personal training stay on. Those on generic pens who cannot get a scan for four months are told by their daughters to stop, and many do. The 'Charlotte build' has spread into Atlanta and Dallas finance as retatrutide came off allocation at $649.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller meals are the default, and full portions now get remarked on. Holiday tables plan around who is on a drug holiday that week. Las Vegas buffets that survived now sell 'tasting passes'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule and now the holiday schedule ('reta, off first weekends'). Nobody discloses being on any more; people disclose being off. 'Clinic pen' as a put-down has faded because almost everyone's pen is a generic.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Every appetite, for food, drink, nicotine, bets or shopping, is treated as dose-responsive. Since the gambling endorsement, losing money on a sports app is spoken of the way untreated drinking was in 2030. Appetite deliberately recovered on a holiday is treated as a small, private luxury.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced pleasure holds at ~10–15% of long-term users across agents. Validated anhedonia shifts in ~7% at retatrutide's top dose against ~2% on placebo (Mar 2031). Planned dose skipping ('holidays', 'Friday skip') is reported by ~30% of long-term users, roughly 15M people. 'Focus' subscription users fell from ~1.5–2M to ~1.2M as generic pens and the complaint undercut the brands.
interior_life.framing: A complaint and a habit of correcting it. 'The grey' is ordinary speech. Clinicians now say 'reward modulation' in the same sentence as 'holiday planning'. Addiction psychiatry calls the same effect the treatment.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Several large employers in finance and logistics quietly dropped 'focus' perks after the 2031 data and the FTC order. Call centres in Phoenix kept them. Sales staff schedule skipped doses before quarter-end. DOT drivers cannot take holidays from tirzepatide without risking apnea clearance, and the Teamsters raised this in bargaining.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is now the mainstream marketing label for new albums and stand-up rather than a niche one. Festivals schedule around the first weekend of the month, when holidays cluster. Sports-betting handle in Nevada, New Jersey and Arizona is softer, and operators lobby against the gambling sNDA.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples coordinate dose holidays the way they once coordinated childcare. Sex therapists ask for the last skipped dose date. Some partners resent a spouse's 'holiday self' as louder, hungrier and more fun.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: State budget offices model lower alcohol, tobacco and gaming excise together, and lottery-dependent states raise it in hearings. Gaming and spirits lobbies fund 'patient choice' groups questioning the gambling endorsement. Candidates are asked whether they are 'on' and when they last skipped.

state.regulatory_posture: Approves supplements and doses (retatrutide 16 mg, MariTide) and lets generics in on schedule. It is more cautious on body composition: the class bone and muscle DSC, the survodutide and amycretin holds. Enforcement against next-gen gray product has escalated to import alerts and one distributor indictment. The FTC polices 'focus' claims.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new state action in the window. Congress passed only clean extenders. The Medicare Bridge continues at $275/$50 through 2032, and HRSA continues under flat continuing resolutions with ~$1.6B unobligated. The ACA cessation mandate and AUD parity apply as before. There is no mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. The three pending state applications sit unapproved at CMS. Cash-paid generics leave no PBM adherence record, so the 13% of users who moved to cash have dropped out of the data employers and Medicaid waivers rely on.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea screening still makes tirzepatide effectively required for some drivers. The Army recruit policy is unchanged. The VA added generic semaglutide to its AUD formulary and began DEXA screening for older veterans on drug.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Generics are exempt from Section 232, so Indian manufacturers supply most US generic semaglutide legally. Tariff fights have moved to branded tirzepatide and retatrutide API. Gray next-gen supply comes from Chinese peptide exporters, and US–China trade talks now include a peptide annex.

events.event: Retatrutide postmarketing study reports dose-dependent anhedonia-scale shifts, clinically meaningful in ~7% of top-dose patients versus ~2% on placebo; FDA adds the finding to the label's adverse reactions and the FTC secures consent orders from two 'focus' subscription brands
FDA approves a 16 mg retatrutide maintenance dose on extension data showing 30.4% mean weight loss at 96 weeks; Lilly lifts allocation in November and prices it at $649 a month on LillyDirect

After a Medicare claims study of 6.1M beneficiaries finds a 42% higher hip-fracture risk in long-term users, FDA issues a class-wide safety communication moving bone and muscle loss into Warnings and Precautions and recommending DEXA for long-term users over 50
ASAM and APA guidelines endorse semaglutide for gambling disorder and extend the alcohol-use-disorder recommendation to tirzepatide; FDA accepts Novo's gambling sNDA and Lilly's AUD sNDA for review

Semaglutide's US compound patent expires and, under earlier settlement terms, Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's and four others launch generic injections alongside a Novo authorised generic; cash prices fall to $45–69 within six months

Federal prosecutors indict a Florida peptide distributor importing Chinese 'research' retatrutide and mazdutide as FDA estimates 3.5M Americans use unapproved next-generation agents, even as compounded semaglutide nearly disappears

open_tensions: Price is no longer the barrier but monitoring is. FDA now recommends DEXA for long-term users over 50, scanners have 3–5-month waitlists, and the cheapest generic regimen is the least monitored. Medicare keeps paying a fixed $275 per Bridge user even for $60 generics, and HRSA sits on $1.6B unspent while still issuing the liraglutide it was contracted for.

The gray market has moved up the molecule ladder. Compounded tirzepatide and Chinese research triples now account for most gray use, while US generics killed gray semaglutide. Enforcement now means trade policy with China rather than letters to telehealth sites.

The same reward modulation is a validated complaint, a cited mechanism for AUD and gambling treatment, and a drag on alcohol, tobacco and gaming revenue that state budgets depend on. The gambling and tirzepatide-AUD sNDAs reach decision in 2033 against active industry lobbying.
Interim registry data hint at reduced adolescent bone accrual in a cohort of ~800k minors, but the FDA calls the data uninterpretable. Final results are not due until 2034.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge still charges a $50 copay with unchanged criteria and a documented DEXA/strength counselling visit for beneficiaries 65+.
HRSA's Community Incretin Access Program still hands out free generic liraglutide at FQHCs against refill pickup alone, with no weigh-ins, and still depends on annual appropriations.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars and a Four-Month DEXA Wait: The Year Being Off the Drug Started Needing an Excuse
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 about fifty-eight million American adults are on an incretin drug, a little over one in five. Fewer people notice it than in 2030. The patent on semaglutide ran out in December 2031. In January eight generic makers and Novo Nordisk's own authorised generic came onto the market, and by summer a month of weekly injections cost between forty-five and sixty-nine dollars at a chain pharmacy. Most of the pens are made in India, and the tariff that repriced branded drugs in 2029 never applied to generics. For many insured people the generic now costs less than their plan's copay, so they pay cash and their insurer never sees the purchase.

Who pays has not changed. Congress passed no new programme. A year-end extenders bill carried the Medicare Bridge forward at the same fifty-dollar copay. Washington still pays plans two hundred and seventy-five dollars a month per Bridge user, including users now filled with a sixty-dollar generic, and nobody has proposed fixing it. The free clinic programme runs on flat continuing resolutions. It still hands out the older liraglutide it contracted for and has more than a billion dollars it has not spent.

The top of the market moved higher. Lilly's retatrutide gained a higher dose in April 2031 that takes off about thirty percent of body weight, the range once reserved for surgery. In November the drug came off allocation at six hundred and forty-nine dollars a month. The gray market followed it up. Compounded semaglutide has nearly disappeared, because the legal generic undercuts it. In its place, telehealth sites sell 'personalised' tirzepatide, and gyms sell vials of Chinese-made retatrutide and mazdutide labelled for research use only. About three and a half million people use molecules no American regulator has inspected. In June prosecutors in Florida indicted a distributor, the first such case.

The bigger story of the window came from Medicare's own data. A study of six million beneficiaries found long-term users forty-two percent more likely to break a hip, mostly women, and mostly those losing weight without lifting anything or eating enough protein. In September 2031 the FDA moved bone and muscle loss into the warnings section of every label in the class and recommended a bone scan for long-term users over fifty. The country does not have enough scanners. In Sun City, Arizona, the wait is four months, so retirees who can afford trainers stay on and many who cannot are told by their children to stop. Use among people over sixty-five has stopped growing.

Two years ago the quieting effect was being sold as a product. Now it is a complaint. A postmarketing study in 2031 measured real loss of pleasure at retatrutide's top dose, and people who had been calling it 'the grey' found the word in a federal label. Roughly a third of long-term users now skip doses on purpose. They skip before a wedding, before a sales close, or on the first weekend of the month, when the festivals schedule their headliners. Couples plan the skipped doses together. Truck drivers can't skip, because their sleep-apnea clearance depends on the drug.

The same effect is now a treatment. In October 2031 the psychiatric and addiction-medicine societies endorsed semaglutide for gambling disorder and extended their alcohol recommendation to tirzepatide, and both applications are now with the FDA. Addiction clinics already prescribe the forty-nine-dollar generic to people losing money on sports apps. Nevada's casinos report guests who spend more at the spa and less at the tables. State budget offices cut their alcohol, tobacco and gaming tax forecasts in the same memo. Spirits makers and betting operators are funding patient groups that question the gambling endorsement.

Seen from outside, the country is leaner and drinks and bets less. Generic prices have nearly closed the gap between rich and poor users. Being on the drug no longer marks anyone. Being off it at forty, heavy, is what people ask about.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosa Delgado skips Thursday. The generic pen stays in the butter compartment, and she tells herself it's for Marisol's quinceañera on Saturday. She wants to taste the tres leches and feel it.

At the Bellagio she cleans fourteen rooms on the twenty-second floor. Housekeeping carts now carry protein bars from the union, a gift from the Culinary Health Fund. Her friend Lupe eats two and says the bars taste like drywall.

At lunch she calls the imaging centre on Charleston. The DEXA slot the pharmacist said she needs, fifty-eight and four years on, is still November. The woman on the phone is kind about it, and the slot is still November.

At home Tomás is on the couch with the phone face down, which is new. The addiction clinic on Maryland Parkway wrote him the same pen she uses, for the betting, and the union plan won't pay for that, so he puts forty-nine dollars a month on the Visa. He hasn't opened the sportsbook app since July. He also hasn't laughed at the Raiders, and she misses the laughing more than she worried about the money.

Thursday night her stomach wakes up around eight. She makes fideo and eats a full bowl, standing at the stove, and doesn't apologise to anyone.

Her daughter texts. Mom you're off this week right? Don't let Tía Carmen say anything.

Rosa sends a thumbs-up and then a cake emoji. Tomás asks what's funny. She says nothing. Then she says, come skip with me Saturday. He thinks about it longer than she expected.
